summary: Can all courses be finished given prerequisite pairs? (Is the prerequisite graph acyclic?)
mainInsight: A schedule exists iff the directed prerequisite graph has no cycle. Kahn's algorithm: repeatedly take courses with indegree 0, remove their outgoing edges, and check that all n courses were processed.

approaches.name: DFS cycle detection (3 colours)
approaches.summary: Detect a back edge using visiting/visited states.

approaches.name: Kahn's algorithm (BFS topological sort)
approaches.summary: Queue of indegree-0 nodes; count processed nodes.

promptVariants: What graph property decides whether all courses can be finished?
options: The directed graph must be acyclic (topological sort / Kahn's)
The graph must be connected so every course can reach every other
The graph must be a tree with exactly one prerequisite per course
The graph must be bipartite so courses split into two semesters
cards.answer: The directed graph must be acyclic (topological sort / Kahn's)
cards.explanation: A cycle of prerequisites can never be satisfied.

promptVariants: Why does `len(order) < n` imply a cycle?
What stays unprocessed in a cycle?
cards.answer: Kahn's algorithm only releases a course when all its prerequisites have been processed (indegree 0). Nodes on a cycle (and anything depending on them) always keep a positive indegree, so they are never enqueued; therefore fewer than n nodes are processed exactly when a cycle exists.
cards.explanation: The same fact gives the order in Course Schedule II.
Each node and edge is processed once.

promptVariants: What data structures does Kahn's algorithm use and what do they cost?
List the structures Kahn's algorithm allocates and their sizes.
cards.answer: Adjacency list O(V + E), indegree array O(V) and a queue O(V): O(V + E) in total.

promptVariants: Why is the edge stored as graph[v].append(u) with in_degree[u] += 1 for [u, v]?
What does decrementing the neighbour's indegree represent?
cards.answer: The pair [u, v] means v must be taken before u, so the edge points v -> u and u gains an incoming edge. When v is processed its outgoing edges are removed: each dependent course loses one unmet prerequisite; at 0 prerequisites it becomes available.
cards.explanation: Mixing up the direction is the common bug.

promptVariants: What if there are no prerequisites?
options: No (a cycle); yes with no prerequisites
Yes, and also yes when there are no prerequisites at all
No (a cycle), and also no when there are no prerequisites
Yes (no cycle exists), but no when there are no prerequisites
cards.answer: No (a cycle); yes with no prerequisites
cards.explanation: 0 needs 2, 2 needs 1 and 1 needs 0: a cycle, so no order exists. With no prerequisites any order works.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Yes, and also yes when there are no prer: The three courses depend on each other in a loop, so it is not schedulable.
incorrectOptionExplanations.No (a cycle), and also no when there are: With no prerequisites there is nothing to violate, so it is schedulable.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Yes (no cycle exists), but no when there: There is a cycle here, and an empty prerequisite list is always schedulable.
